questions.question: What is the difference between an array and a linked list?
questions.answer: Arrays store elements in contiguous memory and allow constant-time indexing, whereas linked lists store elements in nodes connected by pointers and allow efficient insertions and deletions.

questions.question: What is the JOIN operation in relational algebra?
questions.answer: JOIN combines tuples from two relations based on a related attribute.

questions.question: What is a system call?
questions.answer: A system call is a mechanism through which a user program requests services from the operating system kernel.

questions.question: What is asymmetric encryption?
questions.answer: Asymmetric encryption uses a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption.

questions.question: What is partial participation?
questions.answer: Partial participation means some entities may exist without participating in the relationship.

questions.question: What is an object in Python?
questions.answer: An object is an instance of a class containing attributes and methods.

questions.question: Why use abstract classes?
questions.answer: Abstract classes provide a common base and enforce a contract for subclasses.

questions.question: What is the SELECT statement?
questions.answer: SELECT retrieves data from one or more tables.

questions.question: What is read-through caching?
questions.answer: Read-through caching loads data into the cache automatically when it is requested and missing.

questions.question: Can a class implement multiple interfaces?
questions.answer: Yes, a class can implement multiple interfaces.

questions.question: What is multiple inheritance?
questions.answer: Multiple inheritance allows a class to inherit from more than one parent class.

questions.question: What is the Optimal page replacement algorithm?
questions.answer: Optimal page replacement replaces the page that will not be used for the longest time in the future.

questions.question: What is a sliding window?
questions.answer: A sliding window is a TCP mechanism used to control the amount of unacknowledged data in transit.

questions.question: What is the advantage of Bellman-Ford over Dijkstra?
questions.answer: Bellman-Ford can detect negative weight cycles and works with negative edge weights.

questions.question: What is a primary-replica architecture?
questions.answer: A primary-replica architecture consists of one write node and one or more read replicas.
